references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the deaf will hear and the blind will see, which Jesus points to as fulfilled in his answer to John's disciples.
Isaiah describes the messianic time when the eyes of the blind will be opened, the ears of the deaf unstopped, the lame will leap, and the mute will shout for joy – exactly the signs Jesus refers to.
The Lord's servant is called to open blind eyes and lead prisoners out of prison – a messianic prophecy that Jesus fulfills.
Isaiah 61:1 speaks of the Spirit of the Lord being upon the anointed one to preach good news to the poor (πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται), which Jesus directly references.
Isaiah prophesies that the dead will be raised, corresponding to Jesus' words that the dead are raised (νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται).
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus gives the same answer to John's disciples with the same messianic signs.
Jesus reads from Isaiah 61 in the synagogue at Nazareth and declares that the scripture is fulfilled – the same message of good news for the poor, sight for the blind, and freedom for the oppressed.
The context just before this verse shows Jesus' miracles – healing and raising the widow's son at Nain – which are the concrete proofs he asks the disciples to report back to John.
Elisha cleanses Naaman of leprosy, an example of lepers being cleansed (λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται), which Jesus also does as a messianic sign.
Jesus heals a man born blind, a concrete fulfillment of the sign 'the blind see' that he refers to in his answer to John.
